data: Which types of poems had higher arousal scores compared to contemporary poems?

The scatter plot shows three groups of poems: 19th-century poems (circles), Imagist poems (triangles), and contemporary poems (dots). The y-axis represents arousal scores, while the x-axis represents publication years. The caption states that following the Imagist movement, poems scored increasingly lower on emotional arousal. 

To determine which types of poems had higher arousal scores compared to contemporary poems, we need to compare their positions on the y-axis. 

From the figure, it is clear that both 19th-century poems and Imagist poems have higher arousal scores than contemporary poems. The 19th-century poems are generally positioned above the contemporary poems, and the Imagist poems are also positioned above the contemporary poems. Therefore, the answer is:

19th-century poems and Imagist poems had higher arousal scores compared to contemporary poems.
